text:
Mike: FYI ran nsys/perfetto on the longseq regression hitting prod-infer-3. HBM bandwidth spikes at the tail and KV cache eviction rate jumps. Traces attached.

Anya: Can you paste the nsys command + perfetto link? Also which model and seqlen distribution?

Mike: model=gpt-j-6B-quant, seqlen skew with tail up to 4096. nsys cmd I used: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn -o longseq_hotqueue ./run_infer.sh --threads=16 --seq-anchors=4096``` perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/REDACTED_longseq_hotqueue. Timeline snippet: ```Kernel timeline: matmul -> fused_attention_backward -> kv_read_kernel (hotspot ~3.6s into trace) HBM BW snapshot: read 2.1 GB/s, write 0.9 GB/s KV evictions/s: baseline ~312 -> spike ~1892 during tail```

PerfBot: :warning: regression-alert: tailseq-kv-evict spike detected for route/model combo. Throughput -5.8%, p95 latency +120ms. Thresholds exceeded.

Sam: Do we have nvprof/metrics counters from NSYS? Also what's the batching/microbatch config used for that run?

Mike: nvprof-ish counters from the capture: `dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active` ~ 0.42, `sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_max` ~ 0.67. Batching: logical batch 8, microbatching ended up as 1 (single-token streaming).

Lisa: Sounds like a KV readstorm when sequence length balloons. Two quick ideas: 1) increase kv-page prefetch window for predictable longseq traffic, 2) fallback to split-kv prefetch + streaming matmul kernel for tails. Can we repro locally with a synthetic?

Anya: I'll run a synthetic load with skewed seqlen and capture a perfetto trace (DMA + kernel dispatch). Reproducer I plan to run: ```python perf_repro.py --model gpt-j --seq-weights "(0.8:1024,0.2:4096)" --requests 500 --capture perfetto```

Sam: Also check our batching heuristic: maybe it's grouping too many mixed-seqlen requests and creating pathological microbatch token counts. If seqlen variance is high, prefer latency-optimized microbatching. Proposed config snippet: ```yaml batching:   max_microbatch_tokens: 65536   prefer_latency_for_seqlen_above: 2048```

Mike: Quick local experiment: limited max_microbatch_tokens -> HBM spike disappears, p95 drops ~90ms, throughput cost ~-2%. So seems like a tuning/tradeoff problem rather than a kernel bug.

Lisa: Could add a kernel-selection guard: if seqlen variance > X then prefer kernels that avoid aggressive KV prefetch. Avoid prefetch thrash for long tails.

Anya: My perfetto capture shows DMA engine queuing during `kv_read_kernel` and bursts of small page reads that coincide with eviction waves. Screenshot uploaded to thread (link hidden). Suggest trying prefetch stride bump from 128KB -> 512KB to reduce churn.

Sam: Actionable logging: we should emit per-session counters: kv_read_bytes_last5s, kv_eviction_rate, hbm_bw_peak and wire these into the console dashboard for route/model so can set alerts.

Mike: I'll prototype a reactive kv-prefetch backoff: if eviction_rate > 800/s then halve the prefetch window for that session. Pushing a branch `hotqueue-fix` to eng-runtime with a unit test and perf harness.

DeployBot: CI: started hotqueue-fix build. Smoke tests queued. :package:

Anya: After we get a green CI, canary with 5% traffic and capture 24h of metrics (p95/evictions/hbm_bw). If stable, roll to 25%.

Sam: Long-term we should consider putting a kernel-routing metric into Optimize that recommends quant/kernel variants by seqlen distribution per workload.

Mike: Agreed. For now I'll annotate the perf traces and upload the NSYS .qdrep + perfetto. Will also attach the small reproducer scripts.

Lisa: Nice work. If the prefetch backoff reduces evictions with <5% throughput hit we're good. Keep tracker on the ticket: ENGRT-1427.

PerfBot: note: trace artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/longseq_hotqueue/2394012345/ (private).

Mike: Thanks all — hunting the root cause now. Will update thread with canary numbers. :mag:
